pr_body:
~~Fixes #99751.~~ Update: fix for #99751 is already contained in #99602. I'm keeping this PR open for additional verification improvements, though.

When verifying aggregation expressions like `from employees | stats percentile(salary_change, 25*2)`, both arguments are treated the same way during verification. This is incorrect, as `salary_change` is the actual aggregation's field, while `25*2` is merely it's (first and only) parameter. This is overly restrictive.

Apply the current verification only to the aggregation's actual field, as the parameter is already verified during type resolution (it needs to be a constant expression).

issue_context.title: ESQL: NPE when aggregating on literals
issue_context.body:
### Elasticsearch Version

main@b6747b48ba0901a530ba51375e3576fdb8df8527

### Installed Plugins

_No response_

### Java Version

openjdk version "17.0.8" 2023-07-18

### OS Version

Ubuntu 23.04

### Problem Description

`row a = 1 | stats max(1) by a` (or some other agg) results in:
```
Caused by: java.lang.NullPointerException
	at java.base/java.util.Objects.requireNonNull(Objects.java:233)
	at java.base/java.util.ImmutableCollections$List12.<init>(ImmutableCollections.java:556)
	at java.base/java.util.List.of(List.java:812)
	at org.elasticsearch.xpack.esql.planner.AbstractPhysicalOperationProviders.aggregatesToFactory(AbstractPhysicalOperationProviders.java:185)
	at org.elasticsearch.xpack.esql.planner.AbstractPhysicalOperationProviders.groupingPhysicalOperation(AbstractPhysicalOperationProviders.java:133)
	at org.elasticsearch.xpack.esql.planner.LocalExecutionPlanner.planAggregation(LocalExecutionPlanner.java:207)
	at org.elasticsearch.xpack.esql.planner.LocalExecutionPlanner.plan(LocalExecutionPlanner.java:158)
	at org.elasticsearch.xpack.esql.planner.LocalExecutionPlanner.planAggregation(LocalExecutionPlanner.java:207)
	at org.elasticsearch.xpack.esql.planner.LocalExecutionPlanner.plan(LocalExecutionPlanner.java:158)
	at org.elasticsearch.xpack.esql.planner.LocalExecutionPlanner.planLimit(LocalExecutionPlanner.java:520)
	at org.elasticsearch.xpack.esql.planner.LocalExecutionPlanner.plan(LocalExecutionPlanner.java:176)
	at org.elasticsearch.xpack.esql.planner.LocalExecutionPlanner.planOutput(LocalExecutionPlanner.java:259)
	at org.elasticsearch.xpack.esql.planner.LocalExecutionPlanner.plan(LocalExecutionPlanner.java:198)
	at org.elasticsearch.xpack.esql.planner.LocalExecutionPlanner.plan(LocalExecutionPlanner.java:147)
	at org.elasticsearch.xpack.esql.plugin.ComputeService.runCompute(ComputeService.java:204)
	... 147 more
```

@nik9000 's thoughts on this: `I think this is just a kind of special case of "I can't EVAL in STATS". But it's a case the parser accepts.`

### Steps to Reproduce

Run the ESQL query from above.

comments:
I have a fix ready for the NPE itself. The verification of aggs was a bit off and allowed literals.

However, as for actually supporting expressions like `avg(1)` - this will require some work, so I'm going to open a separate issue for this.
Follow-up issue for the enhanced functionality created here: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/99828

Looking at #99602 , it does not seem to make changes to the verifier in its current state, which is (ultimately) the culprit for this bug.

@costin , if that's fine with you, we can leave #99827 open for now and merge #99602 first; I can then re-check and make sure the updated verifier in #99827 still makes sense with the new support for `count(*)`; at least, we should merge the tests that #99827 adds to make sure we do not regress in the future.

#99602 fixes this issue, but doesn't solve the problem of aggregating on literals (entirely, i.e. except count). 

@alex-spies I think we can close this one, but open a new one about [optimising the aggs away](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/c24cc0f54c216a5bff8e6b0e3ad2d09f7a3eb956/x-pack/plugin/esql/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/esql/planner/AbstractPhysicalOperationProviders.java#L242). Wdyt?

@bpintea I agree that we should open an issue on optimizing the aggs away.

However, this is still relevant, even though #99602 improved the current situation by giving a `EsqlIllegalArgumentException` instead of NPE (but still status 500 which is not so nice).

The verifier is still incorrect because it treats aggregation field + parameters the same; for instance, it forbids
```
from employees | stats p50 = percentile(salary_change, 25*2);
```
because `25*2` is not a literal.
Since #99602 fixes the NPE itself and it makes no sense to fiddle with it in #99827, I'm closing this after all.

review_comments:
This leaves the non-field argument verification to each AggregateFunction in part. There are so far just two of these that require an extra param: `CountDistinct` and `Percentile`. I think there's no language restriction that these extra parameters cannot be a some sort of a field and this PR removes that check. However, both of these currently do expect a literal. So I guess relaxing this verifier check is OK.
However, there's a bug in `CountDistinct`, its type resolution not checking if the 2nd parameter is foldable, but then trying to fold it. This check was guarding against that, but with this change we should also fix that -- up to you if you want to do it here or subsequent PR.
That's a good observation. I'll make sure the type resolution in `CountDistinct` is fixed and checked by tests.
